extraction_notes: Common salt incl. iodised — edible NaCl with added potassium iodate; heading 2501 covers all salt regardless of purity. Mineral product, not Ch.28 chemical.
Rock salt (halite) — naturally mined crystalline NaCl, typically grey/pink from mineral impurities.
Other salt — residual basket incl. sea salt, pure NaCl, salt water/brine, denatured salt under heading 2501.
Unroasted iron pyrites (FeS2, 'fool's gold') — Ch.25 covers ONLY unroasted; roasted pyrites (cinders) fall in 2601. Used to make sulphuric acid.
Recovered/Claus-process sulphur from oil refining — crude sulphur of all kinds stays in 2503; sublimed/precipitated/colloidal sulphur moves to 2802.
Other crude/unrefined sulphur incl. native/Frasch sulphur — distinct from refined sulphur of 2802.
Crystalline (flake) natural graphite — 2504 = natural graphite; synthetic/artificial graphite is in 3801. Refractory + electrode use → technical_use.
Amorphous natural graphite — microcrystalline, lower carbon content than flake; used in foundry facings and crucibles.
Other natural graphite in lump/unspecified form under 2504.10.
Micronised natural graphite — ultra-fine ground powder for lubricants/coatings; 2504.90 = graphite other than crystalline/amorphous primary grades.
Other natural graphite under 2504.90 residual line.
Processed white silica sand — high-purity low-iron grade for clear glass. Heading 2505 = natural sands of all kinds, not metal-bearing. Sieve thresholds NULL (none in description).
Processed brown silica sand — higher iron content than white grade, for amber/container glass and foundry. Sieve thresholds NULL.
Other silica sands under 2505.10 — unspecified grade. Sieve thresholds NULL.
Quartz sands — natural sand composed of quartz grains. Sieve thresholds NULL (no granulometry stated).
Other natural sands (non-silica) — e.g. building/construction sands not metal-bearing. Metal-bearing sands excluded to Ch.26. Sieve thresholds NULL.
Quartz in lumps — 2506 = quartz (other than natural sands of 2505) and quartzite. Lump form before crushing.
Quartz in powder form under 2506.10.
Quartzite in lumps — 2506.20 covers quartzite, incl. merely cut into rectangular blocks/slabs. Used in silica refractory bricks.
Quartzite in powder form under 2506.20.
Other quartzite under 2506.20 residual line.
Crude kaolin (china clay) — 2507 = kaolin and other kaolinic clays, whether or not calcined. Crude unprocessed grade.
Pharmaceutical-grade processed kaolin — purified for use as antidiarrhoeal/excipient. Still a mineral product in Ch.25 (not chemically modified).
Ceramic-grade processed kaolin — for porcelain/whiteware bodies.
Other processed kaolin grades — paper/paint/rubber filler.
Crude bentonite — 2508.10 = bentonite (montmorillonite clay). 2508 = other clays, not kaolinic (2507). Used in foundry sand binding and drilling fluids.
Processed/ground bentonite — includes soda-activated grades. Note: acid-activated bentonite would shift to 3802; here treated as mechanically processed mineral clay.
Non-plastic fire clay — 2508.30 = fire clay (refractory clay). Plasticity grades split across the .10/.20/.30 lines. Refractory → technical_use.
Semi-plastic fire clay — intermediate plasticity refractory clay under 2508.30.
Plastic fire clay — high-plasticity refractory clay grade under 2508.30.
Other fire clay under 2508.30 residual line.
Ball clay — 2508.40 = other clays. Highly plastic kaolinitic sedimentary clay prized for ceramic plasticity. Not refractory-specific → intended_role NULL.
Earth clay (common clay) — general-purpose clay for bricks/pottery under 2508.40.
Other clays under 2508.40 residual line.
Andalusite — 2508.50 = andalusite, kyanite and sillimanite (Al2SiO5 polymorphs). Key high-alumina refractory raw materials → technical_use.
Crude kyanite, other than calcined — Al2SiO5 refractory mineral in raw uncalcined form.
Processed kyanite (washed/ground/screened/beneficiated), other than calcined — mechanically upgraded but not heat-treated.
Calcined kyanite — heat-treated (converted toward mullite); 2508 covers these clays whether or not calcined.
Sillimanite lumps — Al2SiO5 refractory mineral. India is a major sillimanite producer (beach-sand derived).
Sillimanite fines incl. sand — fine-grained/beach-sand sillimanite for refractory ramming mixes.
Other sillimanite under 2508.50 residual line.
Mullite — 2508.60. Aluminosilicate (3Al2O3·2SiO2); premier high-temperature refractory phase. Heading covers natural mullite.
Chamotte (fired fire-clay grog) and dinas earth (siliceous refractory earth) — 2508.70. Pre-fired refractory aggregates → technical_use.
Chalk — 2509. Natural soft fine-grained CaCO3. Distinct from limestone (2521) and from precipitated CaCO3 (Ch.28). Tailors'/billiard chalk excluded.
Natural calcium phosphate (unground) — 2510.10 = unground phosphates. Heading 2510 = natural calcium phosphates, aluminium calcium phosphates and phosphatic chalk. Key fertiliser raw material.
Natural aluminium calcium phosphate (unground) — e.g. crandallite-group minerals, under 2510.10.
Natural calcium phosphate apatite (unground) — apatite is the principal phosphate ore mineral.
Other unground natural phosphates incl. phosphatic chalk under 2510.10.
Natural calcium phosphates (ground) — 2510.20 = ground phosphates. Mirror of .10 lines but milled.
Natural aluminium calcium phosphate (ground) under 2510.20.
Natural calcium phosphates apatite (ground) under 2510.20.
Other ground natural phosphates under 2510.20.
Barytes in lumps — 2511.10 = natural barium sulphate (barytes). High-density mineral; primary drilling-mud weighting agent. Distinct from precipitated BaSO4 (Ch.28).
Barytes in powder form under 2511.10.
Other barytes under 2511.10 residual line.
Natural barium carbonate (witherite) — 2511.20. Natural mineral form of BaCO3; distinct from synthetic BaCO3 (Ch.28).
Kieselguhr — 2512 = siliceous fossil meals (e.g. kieselguhr, tripolite, diatomite) and similar siliceous earths, calcined or not, apparent specific gravity <=1. Diatom-skeleton silica.
Tripolite — siliceous fossil-meal variety under 2512; used as filter aid and mild abrasive/polishing powder.
Diatomite — synonym for diatomaceous earth; siliceous fossil meal under 2512.
Other siliceous earths under 2512 residual line.
Pumice stone — 2513.10. Porous volcanic glass; natural abrasive and lightweight aggregate. Heading 2513 = pumice, emery, natural corundum, garnet and other natural abrasives.
Emery — 2513.20. Granular corundum-magnetite rock; classic natural abrasive (emery cloth/paper grit). Abrasive → technical_use.
Natural corundum (Al2O3) — 2513.20. Very hard natural abrasive; distinct from artificial corundum (Ch.28). Abrasive → technical_use.
Natural garnet — 2513.20. Abrasive-grade garnet for waterjet cutting and sandblasting (industrial, not gem). Abrasive → technical_use.
Other natural abrasives under 2513.20 residual line.
Slate — 2514. Whether or not roughly trimmed or merely cut by sawing into rectangular blocks/slabs. Further-worked slate (polished, articles) shifts to Ch.68.
Marble and travertine, crude or roughly trimmed — 2515.11. Apparent specific gravity >=2.5 (heading note). Crystalline CaCO3 dimension stone.
Marble blocks, merely cut by sawing — 2515.12. Rectangular/square blocks. Polishing would shift to Ch.68.
Marble slabs, merely cut by sawing — 2515.12. Rectangular slabs, not yet polished/finished.
Other sawn marble/travertine under 2515.12 residual line.
Alabaster — 2515.20. Calcareous (or gypseous) ornamental stone grouped with ecaussine and other calcareous monumental/building stone in 2515.20.
Other calcareous monumental/building stone (e.g. ecaussine) under 2515.20.
Granite, crude or roughly trimmed — 2516.11. Heading 2516 = granite, porphyry, basalt, sandstone and other monumental/building stone. India is a leading granite exporter.
Granite merely cut by sawing into rectangular blocks/slabs — 2516.12. Not yet polished (polished granite → Ch.68).
Sandstone — 2516.20. Whether crude/roughly trimmed or merely sawn into blocks/slabs. Sedimentary quartz-grain building stone.
Pakur stone — 2516.90. Indian-specific hard basaltic/trap building stone (from Pakur, Jharkhand). 2516.90 = other monumental/building stone (incl. basalt, porphyry).
Stone boulders — 2516.90. Uncut natural boulders of building stone.
Other monumental/building stone (basalt, porphyry, etc.) under 2516.90 residual line.
Pakur stone, crushed or broken — 2517.10. Heading 2517 = pebbles, gravel, broken/crushed stone for concrete aggregate/road metalling. No granulometry threshold stated → sieve fields NULL.
Flint — 2517.10. Pebbles/gravel/crushed flint; used as grinding media in pebble mills and as aggregate. Sieve fields NULL (no threshold given).
Other pebbles/gravel/broken/crushed stone under 2517.10. Sieve fields NULL (no granulometry threshold stated).
Macadam of slag/dross/industrial waste — 2517.20. Road-metalling aggregate from industrial slag. Sieve fields NULL.
Tarred macadam — 2517.30. Crushed stone coated with tar/bitumen for road surfacing. Sieve fields NULL.
Marble granules/chippings/powder, whether or not heat-treated — 2517.41. Made from stones of heading 25.15/25.16; used in terrazzo and as filler. Sieve fields NULL.
Other (non-marble) granules/chippings/powder of heading 25.15/25.16 stones, whether or not heat-treated — 2517.49. Incl. granite chippings. Sieve fields NULL.
Dolomite, not calcined or sintered — 2518.10. Natural CaMg(CO3)2; raw form. Used as steelmaking flux and crude building stone.
Calcined or sintered dolomite — 2518.20. Heat-treated (dead-burnt) dolomite for basic refractory linings → technical_use. Dolomite ramming mix excluded to 2518.30 (not in this list).
Natural magnesium carbonate (magnesite) — 2519.10. Raw MgCO3 ore. Heading 2519 = natural magnesite, fused/dead-burnt magnesia and other magnesium oxide.
Fused magnesia (natural) — 2519.90. Electrically fused MgO; refractory and MgO-insulated heating-element filler → technical_use.
Dead-burnt (sintered) magnesia — 2519.90. High-temperature sintered MgO; principal basic refractory raw material → technical_use.
Calcined magnesia other than dead-burnt (n.e.s.) — 2519.90. Caustic-calcined reactive MgO; not a high-fired refractory grade → intended_role NULL.

Magnesium oxide — 2519.90. Note: heading 2519 explicitly covers magnesium oxide whether or not pure, EXCEPT fused magnesia/dead-burnt which have own lines; pure MgO is here in Ch.25 by heading wording (not Ch.28).
Other magnesia/magnesium oxide under 2519.90 residual line.
Natural gypsum — 2520.10 = gypsum and anhydrite. Land/mined natural CaSO4·2H2O; key set-retarder in cement.
Marine gypsum — 2520.10. Gypsum recovered from marine/seawater evaporite sources; Indian-specific subdivision.
Other natural gypsum incl. anhydrite (CaSO4) under 2520.10.
Calcined plaster (plaster of Paris) — 2520.20 = plasters consisting of calcined gypsum or calcium sulphate. Hemihydrate CaSO4·0.5H2O. Whether or not coloured / with set-accelerators.
Other plasters under 2520.20 residual line.
Limestone flux (L.D. grade, <1% SiO2) — 2521.00. Heading 2521 = limestone flux; limestone used for manufacture of lime or cement. Low-silica metallurgical (Linz-Donawitz) grade.
Other limestone (lime/cement-making grade) under 2521.00.
Quicklime — 2522.10. Calcium oxide (CaO) from calcining limestone. Heading 2522 = quicklime, slaked lime and hydraulic lime, EXCLUDING pure CaO/Ca(OH)2 of Ch.28.
Slaked lime — 2522.20. Calcium hydroxide Ca(OH)2 (hydrated lime) from slaking quicklime with water.
Hydraulic lime — 2522.30. Lime from impure (siliceous/argillaceous) limestone that sets under water; excludes Portland cement (2523).
Cement clinker — 2523.10. Sintered nodules from kiln, intermediate before grinding into cement. Heading 2523 = portland/aluminous/slag/supersulphate and similar hydraulic cements.
White portland cement, whether or not artificially coloured — 2523.21. Low-iron clinker giving white colour for architectural/decorative use.
Ordinary portland cement (OPC), dry — 2523.29. Standard grey hydraulic cement; 'other portland cement' subheading (not white).
Ordinary portland cement, coloured — 2523.29. Grey OPC with added pigment.
Portland pozzolana cement (PPC) — 2523.29. OPC clinker blended with fly ash/pozzolanic material; very common in India.
Portland slag cement (PSC) — 2523.29. OPC clinker blended with granulated blast-furnace slag. Classified under 'other portland cement', not 2523.90.
Other portland cement (incl. rapid-hardening, sulphate-resistant) under 2523.29 residual line.
Aluminous (calcium aluminate) cement — 2523.30. High-alumina cement; rapid-hardening and refractory-castable binder.
Sagol, ashmoh — 2523.90. Indian-specific traditional hydraulic cements/lime-pozzolana binders under 'other hydraulic cements'.
High alumina refractory cement — 2523.90. Calcium-aluminate cement for furnace/kiln linings → technical_use.
Other hydraulic cements (incl. slag/supersulphate cement) under 2523.90 residual line.

Crocidolite (blue asbestos) — 2524.10. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: asbestos is a known carcinogen; crocidolite is the most hazardous amphibole form and is banned/prohibited for import in many jurisdictions incl. India. Trade subject to Rotterdam Convention PIC and DGFT restriction.
Chrysotile (white asbestos) in rock form — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic; trade controlled under Rotterdam Convention and Indian DGFT policy. Serpentine-group asbestos.
Amphibole asbestos in rock form — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: amphibole asbestos (e.g. tremolite/actinolite/anthophyllite) is highly carcinogenic and broadly banned.
Crysolite (chrysotile variant spelling, sic) in rock form — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos.
Amosite (brown asbestos) in rock form — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: amphibole asbestos, carcinogenic and banned in most jurisdictions.
Other asbestos in rock form under 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos, trade-controlled.
Chrysotile raw fibre (beaten/washed/graded to length) — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: processed asbestos fibre, carcinogenic, trade-controlled.
Amphibole raw fibre (beaten/washed/graded) — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic amphibole asbestos.
Crysolite (chrysotile variant spelling, sic) raw fibre — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos.
Amosite raw fibre (beaten/washed/graded) — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic amphibole asbestos.
Other asbestos raw fibre under 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos.
Chrysotile flakes/powder — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos in flake/powder form.
Amphibole flakes/powder — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic amphibole asbestos.
Crysolite (chrysotile variant spelling, sic) flakes/powder — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos.
Amosite flakes/powder — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic amphibole asbestos.
Other asbestos flakes/powder under 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos.
Asbestos waste — 2524.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: hazardous carcinogenic waste; subject to Basel Convention transboundary waste controls plus asbestos prohibitions.
Other asbestos under 2524.90 residual line. RESTRICTED COMMODITY: carcinogenic asbestos, trade-controlled.
Mica blocks — 2525.10 = crude mica and mica rifted into sheets or splittings. Sheet silicate; prized electrical insulator → technical_use. India is a historic mica producer.
Condenser (capacitor) films, trimmed but not cut to shape — 2525.10. Thin mica dielectric films; not yet cut to final shape (cut-to-shape mica → Ch.68). Technical/dielectric → technical_use.
Mica splittings, book form — 2525.10. Thin mica laminae stacked in book arrangement for insulation use → technical_use.
Mica splittings, loose — 2525.10. Loose thin mica laminae for built-up mica products → technical_use.
Other crude mica / mica in sheets or splittings under 2525.10 residual line.
Mica flakes, 2.20 mesh — 2525.20 = mica powder. Coarse graded flake; functional filler grade rather than dielectric → intended_role NULL.
Mica powder, dry ground — 2525.20. Dry-milled mica functional filler.
Mica powder, micronised — 2525.20. Ultra-fine ground mica for cosmetics/coatings.
Mica powder, wet ground — 2525.20. Wet-milled mica retaining high lustre/aspect ratio for premium coatings.
Mica powder, calcined — 2525.20. Heat-treated mica powder.
Other mica powder under 2525.20 residual line.
Mica mine scrap and waste — 2525.30 = mica waste. Feedstock for ground mica powder.
Mica factory scrap — 2525.30. Processing-derived mica waste.
Mica cuttings, book form — 2525.30. Off-cut mica waste in book form.
Other mica waste under 2525.30 residual line.
Steatite (soapstone) block — 2526.10 = talc/steatite not crushed/powdered. Heading 2526 = natural steatite and talc. Block form for carving/machining.
Steatite (soapstone) lumps — 2526.10. Crude uncrushed talc/steatite lumps.
Other uncrushed talc/steatite under 2526.10 residual line.
Crushed or powdered talc/steatite — 2526.20. Includes cosmetic talcum powder, paper/paint/plastic filler grades.

Natural sodium borates and concentrates (whether or not calcined) — 2528.00. Heading 2528 = natural borates and natural boric acid (<=85% H3BO3). Natural mineral form (tincal/borax), distinct from refined borax of Ch.28.
Natural boric acid containing <=85% H3BO3 (dry weight) — 2528.00. Natural sassolite; the 85% threshold keeps it in Ch.25 (higher purity → Ch.28).
Natural calcium borates and concentrates (whether or not calcined) — 2528.00. Colemanite/ulexite-type natural calcium borate ore.
Other natural borates under 2528.00 residual line.
Feldspar lumps — 2529.10. Heading 2529 = feldspar, leucite, nepheline, nepheline syenite and fluorspar. Aluminosilicate flux for ceramic/glass bodies.
Feldspar powder — 2529.10. Ground feldspar for ceramic glaze/body and glass batch.
Fluorspar, <=97% CaF2 — 2529.21. Metallurgical-grade (met-spar) fluorspar; steelmaking flux. The 97% split separates met-grade from acid-grade.
Fluorspar, >97% CaF2 — 2529.22. Acid-grade (acid-spar) fluorspar; principal feedstock for hydrofluoric acid and fluorochemicals.
Leucite; nepheline and nepheline syenite — 2529.30. Feldspathoid aluminosilicate fluxes used in glass/ceramics as feldspar substitutes.
Vermiculite — 2530.10 = vermiculite, perlite and chlorites, unexpanded. Heading 2530 = mineral substances n.e.s. Raw (unexpanded) micaceous mineral that exfoliates on heating.
Perlite — 2530.10. Volcanic glass that expands on heating; unexpanded raw form here. Used as lightweight aggregate and filter aid.
Others incl. powder (chlorites, etc.) under 2530.10.
Kieserite, epsomite (natural magnesium sulphates) — 2530.20. Natural MgSO4 minerals; agricultural Mg/S source. Distinct from synthetic magnesium sulphate of Ch.28.
Meerschaum (sepiolite) and amber, incl. agglomerated, in plates/rods not worked after moulding — 2530.90. Carving/ornamental minerals under mineral substances n.e.s.
Natural arsenic sulphides such as orpiment — 2530.90. Toxic arsenic mineral (As2S3); historic yellow pigment. Natural form in Ch.25.
Calcite — 2530.90. Natural crystalline CaCO3 (incl. optical-grade Iceland spar). Mineral substances n.e.s.

Ores and concentrates of rare-earth metals — 2530.90. RESTRICTED COMMODITY in India: monazite (RE/thorium-bearing) is an atomic mineral; trade/handling controlled by the Atomic Energy Act/DAE. Note: most metal ores are in Ch.26, but RE ores are specifically placed in 2530.90.
Wollastonite — 2530.90. Natural calcium silicate (CaSiO3); acicular mineral used in ceramics and as asbestos-replacement filler. India is a major producer.

Earth colour ochre, crude — 2530.90. Note: most natural earth pigments (ochre/umber) sit in heading 2530 here as Indian-specific lines, though many earth colours are classified in 2821; this tariff places crude ochre in 2530.90.
Other processed earth colour ochre — 2530.90. Washed/ground natural earth pigment.
Strontium sulphate (natural ore) — 2530.90. Celestine (SrSO4); principal natural strontium ore. Mineral substances n.e.s.
Other mineral substances not elsewhere specified or included — 2530.90 residual basket of Ch.25.
